Reviewed both files in context (go.mod uses `go-astiav` — whose cgo directive is `#cgo pkg-config: libavcodec libavdevice libavfilter libavformat libavswresample libswscale libavutil` — plus ebitengine, which explains the X11/asound/mesa dev packages). Overall this is a solid setup: digest-pinned base, SHA-256 + GPG verification of the ffmpeg tarball, `--no-install-recommends`, and layered caching are all right. Here's what I'd improve, roughly by impact:

## Dockerfile

**1. `ENV CGO_FLAGS=...` is a no-op (bug).** Go reads `CGO_CFLAGS`, not `CGO_FLAGS` — your build works purely because `PKG_CONFIG_PATH` points at `/opt/ffmpeg_static/lib/pkgconfig` and go-astiav links via `#cgo pkg-config:`. Drop the line or fix the name. (`CGO_LDFLAGS` is honored but redundant — pkg-config adds the same `-L`.)

**2. No `.dockerignore`.** Context currently ships `.git/`, `bin/`, `vids/`, `state.db`, `.llm-wiki/`. Every repo change busts the `COPY . .` cache, and stale built binaries ride into the builder image. Add one:
```
.git
bin
vids
.llm-wiki
state.db
.vscode
```

**3. Per-package apt pins will randomly break builds.** The base image is already digest-pinned, which is the reproducibility anchor. The `=12.9`, `=1.21.3-1+deb12u1`, `=2:1.8.4-2+deb12u2` pins meanwhile hard-fail the moment Debian ships the next security point release (`+deb12u3` etc. — wget/tar/glibc have had repeated ones). You're betting `apt-get update` never finds a newer `.deb`. Recommend: drop the `=version` pins and rely on the digest (ffmpeg itself is independently pinned via SHA-256, and that's the pin that matters for build stability). If you truly want a frozen apt state, point at `deb.debian.org/debian-snapshot` instead — but that's heavier than you need here.

**4. Clean up the ffmpeg build tree.** The extracted source + objects live in `/tmp/ffmpeg_build` inside the builder — hundreds of MB carried into the `test` stage for nothing:
```dockerfile
  make install && \
  cd / && rm -rf /tmp/ffmpeg_build
```

**5. `yasm` is unused.** FFmpeg hasn't used yasm since ~2016; `nasm` is what matters. Drop it.

**6. Harden the GPG step (reliability, not security).** `keyserver.ubuntu.com` is the classic flaky spot in CI builds — timeouts, IPv6 issues, key not found. Minimal hardening:
```dockerfile
RUN wget -q "https://ffmpeg.org/ffmpeg-release.asc" -O /tmp/ffmpeg-release.asc && \
    gpg --batch --no-default-keyring --keyring /tmp/ffmpeg-keyring.gpg \
        --import /tmp/ffmpeg-release.asc && \
    gpg --batch --no-default-keyring --keyring /tmp/ffmpeg-keyring.gpg \
        --verify ffmpeg-${FFMPEG_VERSION}.tar.xz.asc ffmpeg-${FFMPEG_VERSION}.tar.xz && ...
```
(Importing from ffmpeg.org over TLS avoids the keyserver round-trip entirely.)

**7. Minor: `--disable-debug`** on configure trims lib size; optional.

**8. Expectation note:** the binaries are *not* fully static — `CGO_ENABLED=1` + no `-extldflags "-static"` means glibc/zlib/etc. link dynamically, and Go only passes `--static` to pkg-config when the final link is static. That's fine for running on this host (ebitengine dlopens SDL/X11 libs at runtime anyway), just don't expect to copy them into a minimal container.

## mise.toml

**1. `gotestsum = "latest"` is the one unpinned input in your whole "stable builds" story.** Pin it (e.g. `gotestsum = "1.12.0"`), otherwise the test tool drifts independently of everything you went to effort to freeze.

**2. `DOCKER_BUILDKIT=1` is a no-op** on Docker ≥ 23 (BuildKit is the default). Harmless, droppable.

**3. `--network=host` needs a "why".** Default build networking reaches ffmpeg.org / keyserver / proxy.golang.org fine; host networking is only needed if your machine egresses via the host netns (VPN/proxy). Keep it if so, but comment it — right now it reads as cargo-cult.

**4. Optional:** pin Go in mise to `1.26.4` to match the container, so local `go test` and CI agree; and add `--progress=plain` to `[tasks.build]` for readable logs.

Done — both tasks now run entirely in Docker with the pinned ffmpeg. Summary of this change:

## What changed

**`mise.toml` `[tasks.test]`** — no longer runs gotestsum on the host (which would link volatile ffmpeg); now:
```
run = "docker build --progress=plain --network=host --target test -t img-test-env ."
```
Tests execute during `--target test` image build, so one command is the whole test run, and BuildKit layer caching means a source change re-runs only `COPY . .` + tests — the 13-minute ffmpeg build stays cached. (Corollary: with zero source changes it won't re-run tests; `--no-cache` or a touch is needed to force.)

**`Dockerfile` test stage** — now mirrors your local formatting inside the container, with the version pin kept in sync:
- `ENV GOTESTSUM_VERSION=1.13.0` + `RUN go install gotest.tools/gotestsum@v${GOTESTSUM_VERSION}` (the first path I tried, `gotest.tools/v3/cmd/gotestsum`, 404s — module is `gotest.tools/gotestsum` with main at the root)
- `RUN xvfb-run -a gotestsum --format testdox --format-icons octiicons -- -race -count=1 ./...` — identical flags to your old local task, plus the race detector from the original test stage

The "must stay in sync" coupling between `[tools]` and `ENV GOTESTSUM_VERSION` is called out in comments on both files.

## Validation

`mise run test` → testdox output streamed live, **126 tests in 14.5s, all ✓, exit 0**. xvfb handled the ebitengine packages; race detector on.

One flag: the `build` task currently reads `docker build --network=host --output bin/ ...` — the `--progress=plain` I'd added earlier is no longer in the file (looks like it was reverted since). Purely cosmetic, so I left it as-is. If it was you, fine; if not, it's harmless either way.
